Pipeline

Commands run in this order. Personas never start other personas. The amber rows are decisions only you make.

you decideblue can change filesgrey read-onlydashed only when needed
  1. /specStart spec-driven development — write a structured specification before writing coderepo-recon
  2. You decide: approve spec
  3. /planBreak approved requirements into ordered, verifiable implementation tasksthe session itself
  4. You decide: approve plan
  5. /buildDispatch implementation for one or more planned tasks by workstreamexecutor
  6. /reviewConduct independent review and decide whether a separate VERIFY gate is requiredblind-reviewercode-reviewerdistributed-systems-reviewersecurity-auditor
  7. /testIndependently verify built work when risk or explicit request warrants a separate verifier only when /review requires ittest-engineer
  8. /shipFinal release gate — synthesize review evidence into a GO/NO-GO decision with rollbackthe session itself
  9. You decide: push / merge

Session setup

What every session loads: the rules in AGENTS.md and the pins in settings.json.

AGENTS.md rules
  1. Think Before CodingDon't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.Catches: confidently building the wrong thing.
  2. Simplicity FirstMinimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.Catches: a 200-line solution to a 20-line problem.
  3. Surgical ChangesTouch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.Catches: unrelated diffs that make review impossible.
  4. Goal-Driven ExecutionDefine success criteria. Loop until verified.Catches: declaring success without running anything.
  5. Deterministic Before ProbabilisticCatches: paying latency and nondeterminism for work if/else would do.
  6. Surface Conflicts, Don't Average ThemCatches: inventing a novel pattern nobody chose.
  7. Fail LoudCatches: silent gaps the reader assumes were covered.
  8. Modules Communicate Through ContractsNever reach across a module boundary. Consume the published interface.Catches: hidden coupling that turns every change into a cross-module break.

Self-tests

18 CI steps on every push to main and every pull request. Runs that spend model tokens stay manual.

StepCommand
Preflight — required toolsfor tool in bash git jq python3; do
command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || { echo "missing: $tool"; exit 1; }
done
jq --version && python3 --version && git --version
Hooks — deny, ask, and allow casesEnforcement: the three PreToolUse hooks, deny/ask/allow, including the alias, typo, global-option and quoted-target bypasses (adr/0049).bash dotfiles/tools/tests/test-hooks.sh
Hooks — handoff report gateEnforcement: the SubagentStop handoff gate — complete, partial, claim-only, second attempt, unknown agent, unreadable transcript.bash dotfiles/tools/tests/test-handoff-hook.sh
Hooks — worktree base guardsEnforcement: the two worktree-base guards (adr/0057). Real git fixtures -- bare origin, main checkout, linked worktree, feature branch -- because both hooks decide from git state.bash dotfiles/tools/tests/test-worktree-hooks.sh
Hooks — isolated test runnerEnforcement: the isolated test-runner gate, evidence-gated on the project shipping bin/worktree-test.sh and more than one live worktree.bash dotfiles/tools/tests/test-isolated-test-runner.sh
